prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor workshop viewed from above as the standing camera wearer looks down at a raised stack of yellow-and-white bundled beams on the left (about 0.6–1.0 m away in frames 1–3) and then turns rightward in frames 4–5 toward a darker, lower floor mat (about 1.5–2.2 m away). In frames 1–3, the wearer's bright white lower legs and left arm (0.2–0.7 m below and in front of the camera) reach forward to touch a corded power grinder resting within arm's reach (~0.7–0.9 m) on top of the beam stack, while in frames 4–5 a second person squats on the floor about 1.5–1.8 m ahead and slightly to the left, facing downward away from the camera wearer with rectangular metal tubes within their arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m in front of them) and about 1.2 m away from the wearer's legs. As the wearer turns right and steps slightly back across the 5 frames, the beam stack shifts from the left to the lower-right foreground and is partially occluded by the wearer's legs at the bottom edge, while background equipment (a yellow machine and scale ~2.2–2.8 m behind the crouching worker) enters view at the top. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated height of the foreground beam stack and the wearer's limbs from the recessed floor plane and highlights the raised relief of the grinder and its coiled cord. However, the map is unreliable along thin cord loops that blend into the beam surface and in the far upper background of frames 1–3, where the floor and distant objects collapse into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against the unlabelled workshop floor, beams, and tools, detecting only a small orange block on the floor (~1.5 m ahead to the right in frames 1–2), the camera wearer's extended left arm (~0.3–0.6 m away on the left in frame 3) and right arm/leg (~0.3–0.7 m away at the bottom right in frame 4), and the squatting coworker (~1.5–1.8 m ahead and to the left in frames 4–5) next to a stack of metal tubes (~0.3 m to the coworker's right and ~1.6 m from the wearer). Across the 5 frames, as the camera turns right, the detected regions shift from the floor object on the right of the beam stack (frames 1–2), to the wearer's reaching left arm within arm's reach of the grinder (frame 3), and finally to the squatting coworker facing downward away from the camera with hands reaching the floor workspace (frames 4–5). The masks show partial occlusions and boundary cutoffs where the wearer's arms and legs are truncated by the bottom and right frame edges and where the coworker's bent torso occludes their own lower legs. Beyond RGB, the map provides sharp pixel boundaries separating the crouching coworker's silhouette and the wearer's limbs from the cluttered background mat. However, it is highly unreliable across the strip: it completely misses the wearer's legs in frames 1–3 and 5, misses the power grinder and beam stack entirely, hallucinates a fragmented brown-and-blue 'person' mask on the white beam in frame 4, and misclassifies the orange floor brick as a 'carrot' (frames 1–2) and the metal tubes as a 'book' (frame 5).
descriptions.pose: The pose map plots sparse 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, capturing nothing in frames 1 and 3, a false skeleton on the power grinder in frame 2 (~0.8 m below the camera on the left), and the upper-body yellow skeletons of the squatting coworker (~1.5–1.8 m ahead on the upper left) in frames 4–5 alongside a magenta right-hand skeleton of the camera wearer (~0.4 m away at the bottom right) in frame 4. In frames 4–5, the coworker's head and shoulder keypoints angle downward toward the floor mat and away from the camera wearer, with their left arm in frame 4 and both arms in frame 5 extending ~0.4 m downward to place their wrists within arm's reach of the metal tubes on the floor, roughly 1.2–1.5 m beyond the wearer's foreground right hand. As the camera pans right from frame 1 to frame 5, the tracked coworker enters the upper-left field of view in frame 4 and shifts slightly upward and leftward in frame 5 as the wearer steps back, while the wearer's own body remains mostly out of view below the bottom frame edge. Compared to RGB alone, the pose map explicitly localizes the coworker's shoulder-to-wrist joint articulation under heavy self-occlusion from their hunched posture and maps the finger orientation of the wearer's right hand in frame 4. However, the map is unreliable because it hallucinates a person's torso and limb keypoints onto the inanimate power grinder in frame 2, fails to detect the wearer's reaching left arm and hand in frames 2–3 or feet at the bottom of frames 3–5, and misses the coworker's occluded lower-body joints and fine hand skeletons in frames 4–5.
